SECRET
February 10, 1941.

List of labour agitators actively concerned
in recent labour agitations and who are
now fostering trouble in public utility
companies

1. Yang Ching Nung (楊今農) - Staff member of the
3rd Department (Mediation Department)
of the Shanghai Branch, Social Movement
Direction Committee, 527 Range Road.
He attended Special Branch on December
30, 1940, bringing with him a letter
from the Shanghai Branch, Social
Movement Direction Committee, 527
Range Road, requesting Police co-
operation with the Committee in
bringing about a settlement of the
dispute in the Chung Hwa and Kwang Hwa
Pressing and Finishing Factories.
He was behind the agitation in the
Foo Foong Flour Mill, 126 Mokanshan
Road, in December 1940.

FILE

2. Loo Yoeh Kuo (羅越國) - A committee member of
the 3rd Department (Mediation Depart-
ment) of the Shanghai Branch, Social
Movement Direction Committee, 527
Range Road. He was reported to
be behind the labour agitation in the
Shanghai Gas Company. On
January 8, 1941, he called at the head office
of the Shanghai Tramways and announced
that the Committee did not approve of
the strike of the tramway workers on
January 8, 1941.

3. Yang Shao Yu (楊兆餘), alias Yang Shao-yung
(楊兆熊), ex-conductor No. 288 of
the Shanghai Tramways. Labour
agitator of the Shanghai Tramways. He
was deported on September 17, 1938 to
Swatow. On his return, he was made
Chairman of the "Shanghai Tramway
Workers' Union" and an executive
committee member of the Shanghai General
Labour Union, Lane 95, House 10,
Edinburgh Road, O.O.L. He was
behind the labour agitation among the
local barbers in January 1941.

4. Fang Sieu Ngach (方秀岩) - ex-conductor of the
Shanghai Tramways. Connected with
the Shanghai General Labour Union and

Shanghai General Labour Unions - situation.

With reference to the attached translation of
an extract from the Central China Daily News, dated
5.11.40, on the subject of the "Meeting of Labour
Union Representatives", there are at present two
Shanghai General Labour Unions, one located at Lane
95/10 Edinburgh Road, O.O.L. which is under the
control of the Wang Ching Wei Government at Nanking,
while the other is situated at Lane 247/5 Chung Hwa
Road, Nantao, and was promoted by the Shanghai City
Government in conjunction with local Japanese Military
Authorities. The two unions are opposed to one
another and have been struggling one against the
other for supremacy in local labour as outlined in
reports entitled : "General Labour Movement - independent

Settlement and O.O.L." and "Shanghai Municipality
General Labour Union - reorganisation of Federation
of Labour Unions of Various Trades", dated 16.8.40
and 13.9.40 respectively.

在前市长傅筱庵遇刺身亡后，上海市政府社会局收到南京“社会部”的一项指令，指示位于南市中华路247弄5号的“上海总工会”向“社会部社会运动指导委员会上海分会”办理注册，该分会位于极司菲尔路（今万航渡路）75号，老闸捕房辖区。该指令已转达给相关工会。（上海市政府社会局正扣留原定於1940年10月发给该工会的5,000元补贴。）

Representatives from the Shanghai General

Union, to persuade the latter to effect an amalgamation
with the former union and in consequence an emergency
meeting was held in the offices of the "Shanghai General
Labour Union, Lane 247/5 Chung Hwa Road, Nantao, between
2 p.m. and 5 p.m., November 4, 1940 when the following
resolutions were passed :-

1) That the instruction ordering this union to effect
registration with the Shanghai Branch of the Social
Movement Direction Committee of the Ministry of
Social Affairs be ignored on the grounds that the
various trade and labour unions under the supervision
of this union obtained their sanction and recognition
from the Bureau of Social Affairs of the Shanghai
City Government, prior to the inauguration of the
Social Movement Direction Committee and, therefore,
the existence and functions of the union are legitimate.

2) That an appeal be made to the Central Government,
Nanking, to allow this union to continue to function
independently.

3) That an appeal, in the name of this "Emergency Meeting",
be made to the Bureau of Social Affairs for the issue
of the subsidy which is due.

The meeting was attended by some 125 persons,
representing various trades and was presided over by

CONFIDENTIAL
(Headquarters) Office Notes
Date November 7, 1939
D. C. (Special Branch)
Sir,
In connection with the attached report, I would suggest that in (1) that Mr. Chapelain be approached with the suggestion that he transfer the clerk Chang Kuh Chong to a place where his services would be appreciated. The ex-conductor could be dealt with as in former cases possibly. In (2) I had D.S. McKeown approach Yulin Road Station detectives with the idea of getting the four persons arrested for assault and intimidation in the Ying Foong Silk Weaving Factory strike for possible implication of Ma Ts Tsing, (ex-conductor 478) in the offence, so that we could get rid of him. Yulin Road are applying for a Circular Order of Arrest for him on an intimidation charge, but they have their doubts about executing it in the Eastern District as this man has the Japanese Military Authorities behind him. I think if he could be picked up here we could decide how to deal with him, as it would not, under the circumstances, be politic to put him before the Court. In the 3rd case, I would suggest that the company be prevailed upon to charge those people with assault and thereby remove the reason for the intended strike.
With those leading lights removed a temporary stop would be put to their activities and possibly instil a fear in others wishing to occupy their positions.
C. Crawford
P.A. to D.C. (Sp.Br.)
(批：Seen by D.C. (S.B.))

先生，
关于附件报告，我建议在第(1)项中，向 Chapelain 先生提出建议，将职员张克昌调往其服务能得到赏识的地方。对于那名前售票员，或许可以像以往案例那样处理。在第(2)项中，我让副督察 McKeown 接触榆林路分局的侦探，目的是逮捕在英丰丝织厂罢工中犯有袭击和恐吓罪的四名人员，以便查出马子濬（前售票员478号）可能涉案，从而将其除掉。榆林路分局正以恐吓罪名申请对他发出逮捕通缉令，但他们对于在东区执行此令存有疑虑，因为此人有日本军方当局撑腰。我认为如果能在我们辖区内将其抓获，我们就可以决定如何处置他，因为在当前情况下，将他送上法庭并不明智。在第3个案中，我建议说服公司对那些人提起袭击指控，从而消除预定罢工的借口。

Subject. Labour Movement in Shanghai.
Made by. D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by.

At present three cliques are endeavouring to seize the control of labour movement in Shanghai. They are (1) the Wang Ching-wei Clique, (2) the Japanese Military and (3) the Japanese Naval Authorities. Brief particulars of each clique are given hereunder :-
1. Chung Hwa Labourers' Society (中華工人協會)
This society is sponsored by the Wang Ching-wei Clique with an office at Lane 95, 10 Edinburgh Road. The Chief is Chang Kuh-chong (張克昌), a clerk employed in the Chinese Post Office. North Soochow Road, and concurrently a leading member of the Postal Workers' Union. The society is engaged in buying over former leaders of Kuomintang sponsored labour unions, most of which are now defunct. It has been ascertained that Yang Shao-yu (楊兆宇), ex-Conductor No.288 of the Shanghai Tramways, is also working in the society. He plans to resume operating the now defunct 3rd District Water & Electricity Workers' Union by getting into touch with leaders among the conductors and motormen.
2. Chinese Labourers' Welfare Association (中華工人福利會)
The Special Service Section of the Japanese Military is directing activities of this association, which has an office in Room 106, 20 Canton Road. It is controlled by Ling Ts-chun (林資順), a Formosan, and has a number of former leaders of the now defunct Kuomintang sponsored labour unions.

目前有三个派系正试图夺取上海劳工运动的控制权。它们是 (1) 汪精卫派系，(2) 日本军方，以及 (3) 日本海军当局。现将各派系简要情况分述如下：
1. 中华工人协会
该协会由汪精卫派系赞助，办事处设在爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）95弄10号。负责人是张克昌，他是北苏州路中国邮政局的一名职员，同时也是邮政工人工会的主要成员。该协会致力于收买前国民党支持的工会领导人，其中大多数工会现已解散。经查实，上海电车公司前售票员288号杨兆宇也在该协会工作。他计划通过与售票员和司机中的领导人取得联系，恢复目前已解散的第三区水电工人工会的运作。
2. 中国劳工福利会

CONFIDENTIAL

November 6, 39.

Labour Movement in Shanghai.

At present three cliques are endeavouring to
seize the control of labour movement in Shanghai. They
are (1) the Wang Ching-wei Clique, (2) the Japanese
Military and (3) the Japanese Naval Authorities. Brief
particulars of each clique are given hereunder :-

1. Chung Hwa Labourers' Society (中華工人協會)

This society is sponsored by the Wang Ching-wei
Clique with an office at Lane 95, 10 Edinburgh Road.
The Chief is Chang Kuh-chong (張古昌), a clerk
employed in the Chinese Post Office, North Szechow
Road, and concurrently a leading member of the
Postal Workers' Union. The society is engaged in
buying over former leaders of Kuomintang sponsored
labour unions, most of which are now defunct. It
has been ascertained that Yang Shao-yu (楊少宇),
ex-Conductor No.288 of the Shanghai Tramways, is
also working in the society. He plans to resume
operating the now defunct 3rd District Water &
Electricity Workers' Union by getting into touch with
leaders among the conductors and motormen.

2. Chinese Labourers' Welfare Association (中國工人福利會)

The Special Service Section of the Japanese
Military is directing activities of this association,
which has an office in Room 106, 20 Canton Road.
It is controlled by Wang Ta-chun (王大春), a
Japanese, and has a number of former leaders of the
now defunct Kuomintang sponsored labour unions.

1939年11月6日。

上海劳工运动。

目前有三个派系正试图夺取上海劳工运动的控制权。它们是：(1) 汪精卫派系，(2) 日本军方，以及 (3) 日本海军当局。各派系的简要情况如下：-

1. 中华工人协会

该协会由汪精卫派系赞助，办事处位于爱丁堡路10号95弄。负责人是张古昌（Chang Kuh-chong），他是北四川路中国邮政局的一名职员，同时也是邮政工会的主要成员。该协会致力于收买前国民党支持的工会领导人，这些工会大多已名存实亡。经查证，杨少宇（Yang Shao-yu），原上海电车公司288号售票员，也在该协会工作。他计划通过与售票员和司机中的领导人取得联系，恢复目前已停摆的第三区水电工人工会的运作。

2. 中国工人福利会

日本军方特务机关指导该协会的活动，其办事处位于广东路20号106室。该协会由日本人王大春（Wang Ta-chun，音译）控制，并拥有一批前国民党支持的、现已停摆的工会领导人。

It is at present engaged in organizing local
labourers, especially in the Eastern District. For
this purpose an Eastern District Branch has been
established at 127 Rangoon Road. A temporary
office for the convenience of employees of the
Mechanical Department of the Shanghai Tramways is
in existence at Lane 161, 8 Yuen Fong Road; it is
expected that this office will be amalgamated with
the Rangoon Road Branch. Wong Chi-chong (王啟昌),
aged 25, formerly working in the Fuh Hwa (物華)
Silk Weaving Factory, Chacufong Road (now closed),
and at present Chief of the General Affairs
Department of the Great People's Association, and
Ma Tsing (馬駿) alias Ma Ta-tsing (馬子濬),
ex-Conductor No.478 of the Shanghai Tramways,
are the active leading members. On behalf of the
Welfare Association, Ma is now behind the strikers
of the Ying Foong Silk Weaving Factory, Lane 491,
11 Putmore Road. These strikers are all members
of the Welfare Association.

3. Chinese Republic Labourers' League (中華民國工人同盟會)

The league, situated on Tungcheng Road, Pootung,
is backed by the Japanese Naval Authorities with
Tsui Hsoh-tseng (朱玉珍), ex-Chief of the "Bureau
of Police of the Shanghai Dah Tao City Government"
and at present Officer i/c Pootung Southern District
Administrative Office, as the puppet head. It

该协会目前正致力于组织当地工人，特别是在东区。为此，在兰路127号设立了东区分会。为方便上海电车公司机械部雇员，在袁丰路8号161弄设有一个临时办事处；预计该办事处将与兰路分会合并。王启昌（Wong Chi-chong），25岁，此前在察夫丰路（现关闭）的物华丝织厂工作，现任大同协会总务部主任，以及马骏（Ma Tsing），别名马子濬（Ma Ta-tsing），原上海电车公司478号售票员，是活跃的骨干成员。代表福利会，马某目前正幕后支持普特莫尔路11号491弄英丰丝织厂的罢工者。这些罢工者均为福利会成员。

3. 中华民国工人同盟会

该同盟位于浦东东城路，由日本海军当局支持，傀儡头目为朱玉珍（Tsui Hsoh-tseng，音译），他曾任“上海大道市政府警察局”局长，现任浦东南区行政公署负责人。它

directed the labour agitation among the workers of the
China Printing and Publishing Company Foontung Works
and recently the Addell Brothers Company, 248
Yangtzepoo road. It is learned that the league
is planning to engineer a strike among the employees
of Reuter Brockelmann & Co., 53a Baikal road (a
German firm), whose 100 workers are members of the
league. On September 6, 1939, thirteen workers
were dismissed for assaulting an Indian watchman;
these people agitating that they be reinstated. The
league promised to help them after the termination
of the Addell Brothers' strike.
